libraryPreparationPreflight.agent_guidance: Do not exercise @EnableSpringConfigured, @EnableTransactionManagement(mode = AdviceMode.ASPECTJ), @EnableCaching(mode = AdviceMode.ASPECTJ), or @EnableAsync(mode = AdviceMode.ASPECTJ) through a real AnnotationConfigApplicationContext.refresh(). Spring's ConfigurationClassPostProcessor unconditionally CGLIB-enhances the library's own internal full @Configuration classes (org.springframework.context.annotation.aspectj.SpringConfiguredConfiguration, org.springframework.transaction.aspectj.AspectJTransactionManagementConfiguration, and the equivalent cache/async ones), which calls org.springframework.cglib.core.ReflectUtils.defineClass at runtime and fails under Native Image with UnsupportedFeatureError (verified locally against 6.0.0 with GVM_TCK_LV=6.0.0 GVM_TCK_NATIVE_IMAGE_MODE=current-defaults). This repo's reachability-metadata.json format has no predefined-classes support to register that runtime-defined class, so there is no metadata fix. Instead, cover these aspects the way the existing 5.3.31 suite already does for its passing tests: obtain the aspect via its static aspectOf() accessor (AnnotationBeanConfigurerAspect.aspectOf(), AnnotationTransactionAspect.aspectOf(), AnnotationCacheAspect.aspectOf(), AnnotationAsyncExecutionAspect.aspectOf()) and configure/invoke it directly, or use GenericInterfaceDrivenDependencyInjectionAspect directly, instead of booting a full ApplicationContext through the @Enable* annotations.

input_evidence.summary: #9399 [Automation] native-image run fails for org.springframework:spring-aspects:6.0.0; label=fails-native-image-run; body_chars=8015

risks: Avoiding the ApplicationContext-driven @Enable*(mode=ASPECTJ)/@EnableSpringConfigured flow means the generated test won't cover Spring's bean-registration/@Configuration integration path of spring-aspects, only the direct aspectOf()-based usage — this is an inherent Native Image limitation (runtime CGLIB class definition) with no metadata-based fix available in this repo's format, not a scaffold or dependency gap.

This CGLIB/@Configuration enhancement issue is likely generic to other Spring modules tested under the current stricter native-image default mode, not unique to spring-aspects 6.0.0 — worth flagging if similar failures show up on other spring-* version bumps.
libraryPreparationPreflight.summary: No extra dependency/Docker/env setup needed; flag that Spring-context-driven @Enable*(mode=ASPECTJ)/@EnableSpringConfigured flows CGLIB-enhance library-internal @Configuration classes at runtime and must be avoided in generated tests.
